title: Freeze Agent Core and Security Execution Foundation boundary
purpose: Define the runtime ownership model before implementation so Agent Core orchestration cannot bypass the completed safety substrate.
scope: Define Agent Core as deterministic orchestration, not the model itself.
Define Security Execution Foundation as the only path for side effects.
Map existing MVP modules to their runtime responsibilities.
Document forbidden paths: model-to-tool direct execution, raw shell execution, untracked writes, and secret value retention.
Decide whether AgentCore is initially in-process inside agentd or behind a local Unix socket boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Agent Core responsibilities and non-responsibilities are explicit.
Security Execution Foundation remains the only way to prepare, execute, verify, seal, or roll back effects.
The boundary references existing MVP modules rather than inventing parallel paths.
Distribution Alpha is marked as blocked until the generic Agent run loop is available.
verification: Review architecture docs for direct model-to-tool or planner-to-shell paths.
Confirm all future Agent execution tasks depend on this boundary task.
Run JSON validation for workflow and task files.
risk_notes: If this boundary is vague, later distribution work will accidentally ship hand-written workflows instead of a reusable agent runtime.
